principles: Separate binary availability from reviewer execution readiness.
Prefer observable bounded launchers over silent final-output launchers for reviewer work.
Fail closed for non-human degraded fallback when readiness evidence is missing or contradictory.
Never expose secrets or raw provider transcripts as gate evidence.
Keep old probe events readable but make new gates consume stronger fields.
drivers: User needs operators to see progress/failure instead of waiting on silent commands.
DONE gates consume this as process fact evidence, so schema and registry must change with runtime behavior.
Host CLIs differ: Claude needs --verbose stream-json, agy uses --print/--print-timeout, Codex can have auth failure despite login status.

options.name: A: Extend review_host_availability_probe with bounded launcher-readiness rows and gate on reviewReadyHostCount
pros: One fresh artifact answers both degraded fallback and operator diagnostics
Keeps B-7438 probe/fallback path as the mechanical enforcement point
Can classify wrong flags/auth/silent output without introducing another required command
cons: Probe schema grows and must stay backward-compatible with B-7438 tests

options.name: B: Add a separate review_host_execution_probe command and leave availability probe unchanged
pros: Cleaner separation of version availability and execution readiness
Less risk to existing probe event schema
cons: Degraded fallback would now need two artifacts and operators may run only the weaker one
More gate plumbing and more ways to forget the stronger proof

options.name: C: Only update docs/prompts to recommend Claude stream-json verbose and agy print
cons: Does not mechanically prevent wrong launchers or silent hangs
Repeats the B-7438 self-report failure mode

chosen: A: Extend review_host_availability_probe with bounded launcher-readiness rows and gate on reviewReadyHostCount
rationale: Choose A because the existing degraded fallback gate already requires a fresh host probe; strengthening that artifact gives operators one proof-or-stop surface instead of another optional command. Compatibility can be preserved by treating legacy events as version-only and not review-ready for non-human degraded fallback.

preMortem.scenario: Probe performs expensive live LLM calls by default and burns quota or hangs
preMortem.trigger: Implementation uses full reviewer prompts instead of tiny bounded launcher smoke or help classification
preMortem.consequence: Operators avoid the probe or experience the same long no-output waits
preMortem.mitigation: Use short timeout, tiny prompt, stream/progress-capable modes, and classify metadata separately from optional live execution

preMortem.scenario: Legacy probe events without reviewReadyHostCount accidentally satisfy degraded fallback
preMortem.trigger: Gate falls back from missing reviewReadyHostCount to availableHostCount
preMortem.consequence: A host that only passes --version can still justify single-host fallback
preMortem.mitigation: For non-human degraded fallback require reviewReadyHostCount or valid per-host executionReady rows; missing readiness is not eligible

preMortem.scenario: Launcher registry drifts from actual CLI flags
preMortem.trigger: Agy template remains --prompt-file or Claude stream-json omits --verbose
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers hang or fail after gate says hosts are usable
preMortem.mitigation: Centralize canonical launcher builders and add smoke assertions for Claude verbose stream-json, agy --print/--print-timeout, and Codex auth failure classification

preMortem.scenario: Probe leaks tokens or raw provider output into story process events
preMortem.consequence: Credentials or prompt content enter gate evidence
preMortem.mitigation: Record only bounded labels, byte counts, first progress timing, exit status, and sanitized failureKind/remediation
